description: The bar chart illustrates the average change in compression using two types of frames — “Inferred Frames” (gray bars) and “Observed Frames” (light orange bars) — across five discrete levels of observation probability: 0.2, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, and 0.9. The vertical axis, labeled “Average Change Using Compression,” ranges from -3 to +2, with tick marks at integer intervals, indicating the net effect on compression efficiency (positive values suggest improved compression, negative values suggest degradation). At each observation probability level, the gray bar (Inferred Frames) consistently shows a negative change, ranging from approximately -2.8 at 0.2 to -1.2 at 0.9, indicating that inferred frames generally reduce compression efficiency. In contrast, the orange bars (Observed Frames) show positive values across all levels, ranging from ~0.1 at 0.2 to ~1.8 at 0.5, peaking at 0.5 and then slightly declining to ~1.4 at 0.9, suggesting that observed frames improve compression, especially at moderate observation probabilities. The chart visually emphasizes the trade-off: as observation probability increases, inferred frames become less detrimental to compression, while observed frames maintain a positive but diminishing benefit. The legend at the bottom clarifies the color coding, and the bars are grouped by observation probability along the horizontal axis, with no sorting applied — they are presented in ascending order of probability. No error bars or statistical annotations are present.
